title: NCAA and Modelo partner; Columbia Bank puts name to Washington stadium
article_text:
Modelo, the Mexico-based beer brand, has signed up to become a commercial partner of US college sports' NCAA governing body.

Through a tie-up made public yesterday, Constellation Brands-owned Modelo becomes the first official beer partner of that collegiate sporting body. This adds, in terms of a college sports presence, to Modelo's existing deal with the College Football Playoffs, and its specific individual partnerships with 28 NCAA member schools.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The NCAA is now able to bring alcohol brands in as sponsors (and to have alcohol advertised during its championship events), after a long-running ban was lifted at the start of July. The ban has been lifted as part of efforts to generate an extra $300 million in revenue for the NCAA, over the next six years.

The March Madness high-profile college basketball tournament will act as the centerpiece of this partnership, with Modelo set to advertise around that time period across broadcast, digital, and social media channels.

Modelo will have exclusive rights in the beer category to activate across NCAA domestic broadcasts, while it now also holds rights to use official NCAA marks and logos in its retail programming and consumer promotions.

In addition, the brand will activate at select NCAA championship events, as well as in "priority markets."

Finally, Modelo now holds exclusive ready-to-drink (RTD) sponsorship rights. As such, RTD brand SpikedAde – bought up by Constellation Brands last month – will be promoted.

Mallika Monteiro, executive vice president and managing director of beer brands at Constellation Brands, commented: "Few things inspire the pride, dedication and fighting spirit quite like we see in college sports fans, and Modelo has spent years building a presence alongside them at the biggest moments."

Outside of college sports, Modelo also sponsors multiple Major League Soccer franchises, including Inter Miami, Atlanta United, and LAFC.

Earlier this year, it sponsored coverage of soccer's 2026 FIFA World Cup – held across Mexico, the US, and Canada – on US Spanish-language broadcaster Telemundo.

In terms of NCAA activity, meanwhile, late August saw the organization announce a wide-ranging new agreement with the sports media and marketing technology firm Playfly Sports, which has now become an NCAA sponsorship sales agent.

Elsewhere in college sports, the University of Washington, in that US state, has brought in Columbia Bank as the new title sponsor for its college football program home stadium.

That venue – from January 1 – will be called the Columbia Bank Stadium, while the bank has also become the fourth 'signature partner' – the top level of sponsor – for Washington University. It joins Pepsico, Starbucks, and Alaska Airlines, as a signature partner.

Columbia Bank has become an exclusive partner of the Washington Athletics program, in addition.

It also plans to engage with student athletes there around financial education and management.

The university has worked with the One Roof Sports & Entertainment agency to develop the partnership deal.

Robert J. Jones, president at the University of Washington, commented: "This is the kind of partnership great public universities should be building. It brings together two institutions with deep roots in Washington and creates opportunities that extend well beyond athletics."

title: Euroleague and Motorola take partnership into fourth season

title: How the BBC is using AI to transform live sport – and why it’s licensing the tech to rivals
article_text:
The BBC is one of the most influential organisations in the history of broadcasting. For more than a century, it has pioneered new technologies and content formats, establishing a reputation for technical and programming excellence around the world.

This is thanks in no small part to an internal research and development (R&D) team tasked with identifying innovations and making them fit for purpose. This can range from a more cost-efficient form of transmission or a new product that transforms the viewing experience.

Ultimately, it’s about delivering value to the British public who fund the BBC through the universal licence fee.

“We’re really focused on how we use new technology and how it will impact audiences,” Eleni Sharp, head of product, BBC Research and Development, tells SportsPro. “We look at audience trends and behaviours as well, and we work with content brands across the BBC and beyond and really try and imagine and prototype and develop what could be next.

“That might be a new piece of technology. A few years ago, it was extended reality and now obviously it’s artificial intelligence (AI). We will [investigate] what these technologies mean for the BBC and how [we] can use it.

“We also obsess about audience behaviour and look at how audiences are using technology [and] what the behavioural trends are.”

These investments have an impact beyond the walls of W1A. They have raised standards across the industry and created new markets for commercial rivals to take advantage of. The BBC’s early adoption of streaming and podcasts helped popularised both among British consumers, and many of its insights are shared through standards bodies, conferences and academic papers.

While other sections of the media might accuse the BBC of mission creep and argue that the licence fee gives it an unfair advantage, that funding stimulates the entire broadcasting ecosystem, both directly and indirectly – in the UK and beyond.

Inevitably, a key focus for Sharp and her team right now is AI. Areas of interest include how it can help the BBC attract and serve audiences in an era of unprecedented choice, as well as drive backend efficiencies that deliver the greatest value to the licence fee payer.

“[AI] is able to fast-track a lot of the things that we want to do,” Sharp explains. “Editorial teams can re-version content very quickly. Transcription and translation previously took journalists and editorial teams a long time to do. It’s so quick that they can do other things as well and we can offer more services to audiences.

“From a creative perspective, it’s just been amazing … we can prototype and build quicker than ever, bringing something to market for trial. Obviously, when we then want to do it at scale, on multiple devices, for the BBC, that [process] will take longer.

But we can actually test things out and validate them quicker than ever, which is brilliant. It’s a brilliant time to work in research and development.”

In sport, personalisation is seen as essential for any rights holder or broadcaster seeking to maximise engagement and revenues. Data and intelligent algorithms tailor the experience for individual users, encouraging them to spend more time in a particular digital environment.

The BBC has created ‘Signals’ – a digital platform that allows broadcasters to add various layers, such as real-time data, AI, commerce and gamification elements on top of a live video feed, personalising the experience for individual viewers. This fusion of personalisation and interactivity effectively combines the first and second screen, ensuring viewers are as engaged as possible with what they are watching, rather than checking a mobile app.

This deepens fan relationships, increases watch time and plugs value leaks by ensuring rights holder and rights owner receive the full benefit of that engagement – rather than a social media platform or mobile app that hasn’t made an investment.

There have been many experiments with object-based broadcasting, whereby different video, audio and graphic feeds are transmitted in a modular fashion and reassembled depending on the end user’s preferences. However, the advent of digital distribution and embedded intelligence means it is nearing reality.

Signals was used for every live BBC broadcast from Wimbledon’s Centre Court during this year’s Championships. Some of the layers added to the live feed included data-driven graphics, such as player dominance and serve speed, animations celebrating record-breaking moments and two-way editorially generated quizzes.

Sharp suggests this interactivity layer could even influence the questions asked during post-match interviews, bringing viewers closer to the content they are watching. A voice-activated AI assistant trained on tennis and Wimbledon data, which was also built for the tournament, could amplify this personalisation even further, as could other applications of AI.

“We want to move audiences from information to conversation,” says Sharp. “AI will explain key moments, generate content, allow audiences to catch up, and help people understand and make recommendations as to what they would like to watch next.

“We had really great audience feedback … the average amount of time that people spent was 30 minutes and four seconds, which was more than we expected. We also saw that 75 per cent of viewers chose to keep Signals enabled even when they had the option [to turn it off].

“But really, this is just the start of what we’ve got planned.”

Sharp has already identified other sports and plenty of future additions for Signals: “Football, athletics, cricket, and motorsport are all really obvious fits. We can reuse the player cards, key moments and race statistics, and we can design the interface to complement [whatever] we’re working with.

title: 2026 ATP Finals: The business behind tennis’ US$15.75m prize
article_text:
The 2026 ATP Finals will bring the curtain down on a men’s tennis season headlined by breakout campaigns for American players and the prolonged absence of some of its biggest stars.

Carlos Alcaraz returns from injury to pursue his first ATP Finals title, but his great rival Jannik Sinner will miss the tournament while he continues his recovery from a knee problem.

With last year’s champion Sinner out of contention, Germany’s Alexander Zverev – who won his first major title at Roland-Garros before claiming the US Open in September – is guaranteed to finish 2026 as the world number one. Alcaraz is too far adrift to catch him, even if he goes unbeaten in Turin and collects the maximum 1,500 ranking points available.

Still, there is plenty to play for at the event, which will once again offer record prize money, underlining its status as the most lucrative tournament outside the Grand Slams.

Since 2021, the ATP Finals have been held at Turin’s Inalpi Arena, which was built to stage ice hockey events at the 2006 Winter Olympics. The city beat off competition from Manchester, Singapore and Tokyo in 2019 to secure a five-year contract until 2025, taking over hosting duties after a hugely successful 12-edition stint in London.

Speculation that the event could move to Saudi Arabia was quashed by an extension signed in 2024, though this only guaranteed it would stay in Italy until 2030.

Despite some suggestions that the Finals could relocate to Milan, the ATP has confirmed that Turin will continue as host in 2027. Its case will have been strengthened by several upgrades on show this year, including an increase in capacity from 12,000 to 13,500 seats, new hospitality areas and an open practice court in the fan village.

Organisers will be hoping that the absence of home favourite Sinner does not dent ticket sales after a record 229,879 spectators attended in 2025, up nine per cent on the previous year. Either way, the event has proved prosperous for the host city, reportedly generating an economic impact of almost €600 million (US$663 million) in 2025.

Italy is also returning as the host of the under-21 Next Gen ATP Finals, which will take place in Reggio Calabria from 9th to 13th December, cementing the country’s association with both of the tour’s season-ending tournaments. The move was announced in September, ending the ATP’s search for a new home for the junior event after its contract with Jeddah, due to expire in 2027, was terminated prematurely.

The total prize pot for the 2026 ATP Finals is a record US$15.75 million, an increase of US$250,000 from last year. An undefeated singles champion can take home a maximum of US$5.171 million, while an unbeaten doubles team will earn US$959,300.

The ATP Finals purse was on par with the WTA Finals last year, but it is now US$5.75 million bigger. The women’s tour’s season finale saw its prize pot fall to US$10 million after its hosting deal with Saudi Arabia ended early and the tournament was moved to Indian Wells.

However, the ATP was looking enviously at the WTA when the women’s tour secured a US$14 million pot as part of its ill-fated deal to take its season-ending competition to Shenzhen from 2019. Indeed, the move from London to Turin was partly motivated by improved finances.

Thanks to support from title sponsor Nitto and the Italian government, the prize fund has increased by 75 per cent from US$9 million in London to the current figure. It could continue to grow in the coming years, with the Italian Ministry of Sport committing US$100 million to support the event until 2030.

Title sponsorship for the ATP Finals is arguably the most prized inventory on the circuit.

When the ATP was considering moving to London back in 2009, the support of banking giant Barclays, which was seeking to diversify its sponsorship portfolio away from soccer, was vital. Despite the deal nearly collapsing due to the financial crisis in 2008, the eight-year partnership was renewed twice and was hugely successful.

Japanese electronics firm Nitto replaced Barclays in 2016, signing a five year-extension in 2020. Last year, the company renewed the deal until 2030.

Meanwhile, the Emirates airline, coffee company Lavazza and car manufacturer Lexus are all platinum partners of the event, which also benefits from the support of a portfolio of gold, silver and bronze sponsors, as well as official suppliers like TechnoGym and TicketOne. One of those silver partners is yoghurt brand Fage, which recently became the title sponsor of the WTA Finals.

More broadly, the ATP said ahead of the Finals that the tour’s central sponsorship revenue increased by a record 49 per cent this year, taking it past the US$100 million mark for the first time. The growth was attributed to continued investment from existing partners and new deals with EQT, K-Swiss and Julius Baer, which became the ATP’s first official wealth management partner earlier this week.

The ATP Finals are typically among of the most-watched events of the season, with the prospect of eight days of competition between the world’s best players an obvious draw for viewers.

That was certainly the case last year, when more than 6.7 million viewers in Italy watched Sinner pip Alcaraz to the championship across pay-TV network Sky and public service broadcaster Rai, making it the most-watched tennis broadcast in Italian television history.

Those numbers will be hard to match without Sinner, but could get a lift if Italian debutant Flavio Cobolli puts together a strong run. Still, the withdrawal of last year’s champion is a blow for Mediaset, which prised the free-to-air rights away from Rai in a new deal reportedly worth €4 million per year.

title: Dusting off F1 blueprint, Liberty Media switches MotoGP media rights to ESPN in America
article_text:
Liberty Media is switching MotoGP’s U.S. broadcaster to ESPN in 2027, as the motorsports operator looks to the same media network that was with F1 during its boom period to unlock growth for the motorcycle racing property. The agreement is for two seasons and was announced this afternoon without financial terms included. A change for MotoGP hadn’t previously been reported to be in the works.

However, the series has been doing short-term deals in recent years as it seeks to grow from a low viewership base in America that is sizably less than what F1 was getting when Liberty bought F1 in 2016. Some races get as low as five figures in viewership and typically not higher than the low six figures in America, a base that Liberty hopes to quickly lift.

Liberty acquired what is now formally called the MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group last year. MotoGP was most recently with Fox Sports in the last two campaigns but it was with TNT Sports and NBC Sports in the handful of years before that.

Range Sports advised MotoGP on the deal.

The agreement is only for linear streaming channels in the U.S., but it also includes a linear plus Disney+ streaming component in some Latin American markets that ESPN also will now air MotoGP in. ESPN is not announcing exactly which of its channels the races will air on today, and it said some will be on tape delay.

MotoGP and ESPN’s relationship in Latin America dates back to 2002, the sides said. ESPN will be able to sub license some of the races in Argentina and Brazil to free-to-air broadcasters.

Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez is closing in on winning the 2026 MotoGP championship with two rounds left. title: Chiefs turn to HNTB as architects for new stadium
article_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs, of American football's NFL, have tied up with engineering and architecture firm HNTB, as plans for their new stadium continue to take shape.

Through a deal unveiled yesterday, HNTB will serve as the official architect for the Chiefs, who plan to move to their new home in Wyandotte County, Kansas, in 2031.

HNTB is now working alongside the Chiefs and the design experts inside the NFL organization to "make it a one-of-a-kind destination for Chiefs Kingdom."

This news comes a day after it was disclosed that the Clark Construction Group, and AECOM, will be involved in building the new venue.

Construction on the 70,000-capacity stadium is set to begin next year, with the project expected to cost around $3 billion.

The Chiefs have played at the iconic Arrowhead Stadium – the oldest venue in the American Football Conference – since construction was finished in 1972.

Mark Donovan, president of the Chiefs, commented on the agreement: "With more than 100 years of infrastructure design, planning, and management experience, HNTB has long been a leader in delivering projects with significant impact, and the work that we accomplish together over the next five years will be no different."

Tom O'Grady, HNTB's president, added: "Becoming the official architect of the Kansas City Chiefs creates new and unique opportunities to build on our collaborative vision, for both the new stadium and the programs that connect with Chiefs Kingdom and the broader Kansas City community. We are excited about what we will accomplish together in the years ahead."

The Chiefs unveiled that they will be leaving Arrowhead last December; following the conclusion of the 2031 campaign, that venue will be demolished.

Arrowhead Stadium is located inside Kansas City's Truman Sports Complex – that site also houses baseball's Kansas City Royals, who play their home games at Kauffman Stadium.

The Royals are also aiming to leave their home ballpark by 2031, and are planning to move to a new, 34,000-capacity venue in downtown Kansas City.

Late October saw the Major League Baseball franchise unveil Legends Global as the owner's representative for the project.

The Royals have also recently announced Australian design firm Populous as their architect of record.

title: Tour winner defends harsh criticism of LIV pros: 'Shouldn't we just follow the rules?'
article_text:
Two-time PGA Tour winner Erik van Rooyen is fighting to keep his PGA Tour card at this week’s Austin Championship. It’s a tall task any year, but it may be even more difficult in the next two years.

With the fall of LIV Golf, many players from the upstart league will start to funnel back into the DP World Tour and, eventually, the PGA Tour, competing for a limited number of Tour cards with players who stayed loyal to those tours.

While the path back to the PGA Tour is much tougher than the avenues to the DP World Tour, van Rooyen doesn’t think it’s tough enough.

He made his feelings known in a recent interview with Golfweek. Then on Thursday at the Austin Championship, van Rooyen doubled down on his criticism in his post-round press conference.

Van Rooyen’s initial comments came shortly after news broke that LIV Golf was officially over. That development turned hypotheticals about waves of LIV pros returning to golf’s traditional tours into a sudden reality.

Former LIV Golf pros will have to pay a penalty and likely serve a one-year suspension before returning to the PGA Tour, but once they do, some will be eligible for PGA Tour status based on past performance. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp has not yet decided on what the path back for LIV defectors will be.

In his interview with Golfweek last week, van Rooyen criticized that fact, arguing instead that ex-LIV pros should be forced to “go back to Q-school.”

“We were told initially that if you played LIV, you would be banned from the PGA Tour, and the story just kept changing,” van Rooyen told Golfweek. “They gave the finger to the Tour. If you’re that good, go get it done.”

One week later in Austin, van Rooyen stood by his harsh criticism in a press conference after an opening-round 64 that put him within two shots of the early lead.

When a reporter asked if van Rooyen had received any “blowback” from his controversial LIV opinion, the pro answered in the negative.

“What kind of folks? No, no one that I hang around with. It might be people I don’t know on social media,” van Rooyen said, referring to any possible critics of his position.

He then qualified his original comments, arguing that certain major-winning stars should be exempted from returning to Q-school to regain their Tour status.

“I made a comment about saying guys should go back to Q-school. I think it’s completely status dependent, right?” van Rooyen explained on Thursday. “Like Jon Rahm has no reason to go back to Q-school, you know what I mean?”

But van Rooyen reiterated that most other former LIV players shouldn’t automatically be granted Tour status. He used his own playing career as an example.

“If a player in my position went and played Sunshine Tour for two years, I’d lose my rights to play here, so I would have to go to Q-school and find my way back, right? So isn’t that fair?” he asked.

Ultimately, he claimed he didn’t have any personal grudge against LIV players. He just thinks they should follow the rules.

“I have nothing against players that went to LIV, nothing personal at all,” van Rooyen said. “But that’s just how things work, right? So shouldn’t we just follow the rules?”

It’s unlikely van Rooyen’s opinion will change the PGA Tour’s plan for LIV pros. But if he can pull off a victory this weekend in Austin, he won’t have to worry about any of those players stealing his spot on Tour any time soon.

title: Carlos Alcaraz delivers ATP Finals injury update as he picks a high-profile rival for practice session
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has served up a positive update on his fitness ahead of the ATP Finals, even though his right knee was still strapped during his latest practice session.

The Australian Open champion has had a hectic few weeks of action, with his title win at the Vienna Open backed up by a big win at the Paris Masters.

Now Alcaraz is targeting his first ATP Finals title and he has arrived in Turin with some concerns over the condition of his right knee.

Alcaraz’s knee was strapped and taped during first practice session on Wednesday, but he appeared to have full range of movement.

Now he has returned to the court for a second day as he staged a competitive practice session with world No 1 Alexander Zverev, which included some competitive points at the end of the session.

The tape was not on his knee for the session with Zverev, but there was some white tape present as he went through his paces.

A small set of spectators were fortunate to watch the two top seeds at the ATP Finals do battle, in what could be a prelude to the final of the competition that gets underway this Sunday.

Alcaraz appeared to be walking and moving with freedom and showed no signs of pain as he exchanged blows with Zverev, with the duo confirming they are on friendly terms as they exchanged a warm embrace at the beginning and end of their hitting session.

With his big rival Jannik Sinner out injured, Alcaraz will be eager to win his first ATP Finals title and he was in an upbeat mood as he looked ahead to the battle in Turin following his Paris Masters win last weekend.

“Well, obviously the ATP Finals is, you know, the best eight players in the world,” said Alcaraz after his win against Shelton in the French capital.

“It is a really important tournament for everybody. That’s what we are working for and making a really good position to start the year the best that we can, and playing during the whole year the best that we can to qualify to that tournament.

“So that means, you know, we just put extra motivation, extra energy to come into that tournament. As I said openly, this is a tournament that I really want to win one day.

“I don’t know if it’s gonna be this year, next year, if I ever gonna be able to win this tournament, but I’m gonna work hard.

“I’m going to believe that I can do that, and, you know, I’m going to go this year with a lot of confidence. I’m going to go for it, for sure.”

title: Blitzboks in final stretch as HSBC SVNS loom large
article_text:
The Blitzboks are in their final two weeks of preparation for the forthcoming season and the anticipation of getting their title defence underway is exciting.

The Blitzboks will travel to Dubai on Monday 23 November for the opening leg of the 2027 series, to be held at The Sevens on 28 and 29 November, with the HSBC SVNS Cape Town a week later.

Snyman will name his 13-player squad for Dubai next Friday, but until then, he will keep a watchful eye on a large training group that include all but two of the 2026 squad that won both the HSBC SVNS Series and World Championship double.

Mfundo Ndhlovu and Donavan Don have left the squad for Vodacom United Rugby Championship opportunities, while Impi Visser, Zander Reynders, Jayden Nell and Shilton van Wyk is busy with rehabilitation and will miss the opening leg of the new season.

Like last season, when he blooded six new players, Snyman is looking to do more of the same, but said the focus for the season will change slightly.

“With Olympic Games qualification determined by the final placings of the 2027 World Championship tournaments, we will make sure we have our best team ready for those events, and to be able to do that, we will use the first six tournaments of the series to build depth and cover in certain crucial positions,” Snyman said from their Stellenbosch training base on Tuesday, after yet another tough session in hot conditions.

“Most of our established group of players are fit and ready, apart from the four injured players, while we also invited some very exciting younger talents into camp.

“There are a number of players who played for the Junior Springboks over the last two years, while some standouts in the FNB Varsity Cup were also drafted into this group. We also have some loan players from the franchises, such as JC Mars from the DHL Stormers, who are training with us.”

The Blitzbok coach is pleased with the energy and talent on display.

“No one in the contracted group is resting on their laurels, while the new players are pushing hard for more permanent opportunities and that delivers a very competitive environment.”

Snyman is set to split the squad in two smaller groups, one with focus on the HSBC SVNS event, while the second group will also travel to Dubai to play in the International Invitational Tournament.

“We have seen in the past how important that tournament is for our younger group as they also have international teams playing in that tournament, and it also gives them a real feel of tournament play,” he said.

title: Anthony Kim reveals why he picked LIV Golf over the PGA Tour and comments on his future
article_text:
Anthony Kim produced what was arguably the best moment in LIV Golf's history in Australia earlier this year.

Kim fired a final-round 63 at LIV Golf Adelaide after getting the better of Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm down the stretch to win his first professional tournament in almost 16 years.

The 41-year-old had actually lost his LIV Golf card in 2025, before earning it back ahead of the 2026 season.

Anthony Kim's off-course struggles and his turbulent personal life have been well-documented, but it's fair to say that he ended up being one of the biggest success stories on LIV Golf.

Kim's incredible comeback win at LIV Golf Adelaide was the culmination of some seriously hard work and an inner belief that cannot be taught.

The American's last win before his victory in Adelaide came on the PGA Tour in April 2010.

With LIV Golf now on the brink of complete collapse, could we see Anthony Kim tee it up at a PGA Tour event once again at some point in the future?

While speaking on his YouTube channel, Kim explained his reasoning behind his move to LIV Golf back in 2024.

"I have gotten quite a few questions about why I played on LIV and decided to take this opportunity," Kim said.

"One was that part of my rehab process was to be outside. It gave me a great opportunity to work on my sobriety while getting to do something that I was once good at. For that I will always be grateful because sobriety, my family and God are the most important things in my life.

"The relationships I have built and have after being so broken are very key to my growth and my success, so being a part of LIV was something great for me at the time and I know obviously with LIV shutting down I am going to have to find a new path.

"But whatever that path is, I am grateful that I got to be back in the game of golf and obviously making a difference in the world. Hopefully it is more than one person, but if it's just one person it is still worth it."

Anthony Kim's reasoning for joining LIV Golf makes total sense. He is actually one of the very few players to come out of the failed project with his head held high.

It will now be fascinating to see what he does next. Will he return to the PGA Tour one day? Or will he focus on other things?

Only time will tell, of course, but whatever happens, Anthony Kim always provides completely raw and unfiltered entertainment.

And that is what we want to see from our sports stars.

title: Kumamoto Masters: Sen Stays in Sight of Hangzhou
article_text:
HYLO Open champion Lakshya Sen’s recent form continued to hold as he made the semifinals of the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026.

The Indian did himself a big favour for his chances of qualifying to the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 in Hangzhou as he beat home hope Yushi Tanaka 21-16 21-15 to set up a last-four clash with No.6 seed Alwi Farhan, who has already qualified for the season finale.

Two others in contention for Hangzhou – Kunlavut Vitidsarn and Koki Watanabe – will face off in the other semifinal.

In men’s doubles, Arctic Open champions Aaron Tai/Yap Roy King made their third semifinal from five tournaments, as they blew past Lee Jhe-Huei/Yang Po-Hsuan 21-16 21-12. The Malaysians take on Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard, who are among the frontline contenders to qualify for the season finale. In the top half, new combination Wang Chang/Xie Hao Nan face home duo Takuro Hoki/Yugo Kobayashi, who beat No.7 seeds Ben Lane/Sean Vendy in an hour-long quarterfinal.

The mixed doubles will see Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi – who are still in the reckoning for Hangzhou – take on in-form pair Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin, while the other semifinal features Akira Koga/Natsu Saito against Gao Jia Xuan/Wu Meng Ying.

title: Coca-Cola, O2, Rolex: Building Successful Sport Sponsorships
article_text:
Sports sponsorships can be a huge opportunity for businesses – and the market is only growing.

According to valuations from Fortune Business Insights, the global sports sponsorship market size is projected to grow from US$99.73bn in 2026 to US$181.38bn by 2034 – showing a CAGR of 7.76%.

But simply increasing spend on sports sponsorships will not automatically lead to a higher return on investment.

- US$99.73bn -> US$181.38bn: The global sports sponsorship market size is set to grow significantly between 2026 and 2034 (Fortune Business Insights)

Modern brand alignment asks leaders to ensure they have a clear strategy when it comes to investing in sport – with authenticity, long-term investments and positive community impacts helping ensure that a sponsorship can better resonate with consumers.

Companies can easily fall into the trap of pursuing broader audience reach, leaving authentic brand identity by the wayside.

When entering into a sports partnership, it can be much more valuable for business leaders to focus on ensuring that partnership is closely aligned with their brand’s overall mission and values – instead of seeking out isolated spikes of popularity.

Taking this approach can create a much more organic alignment, meaning that a company can better resonate with its target audiences. A mismatched partnership, meanwhile, can risk alienating existing customers, and may not even secure any new ones.

This can be even more detrimental when the upfront cost is so high. According to SponsorUnited's “State of the Market: Marketing Partnerships” the average professional sports team sponsorship deal in North American markets is now close to US$1m – meaning that businesses need to protect a significant capital investment when they make the decision to enter into a sports sponsorship.

Therefore, brands and business leaders need to focus on more disciplined messaging, and carefully curated partnerships that reflect their core values rather than chasing fleeting trends.

While short-term sponsorship deals can produce temporary surges in brand awareness, they often don’t build an established brand association between the sport and the company. To achieve that, companies need sustained exposure across multi-year cycles.

In fact, isolated matchday and broadcast presence is no longer enough. According to PwC’s 2026 Global Sports Survey, 78% of executives are prioritising diverse revenue streams – with capital moving towards clubs that have stronger commercial infrastructure.

Extended partnerships allow companies to get more involved in the actual operations of a sport and, over time, a continuous presence can help convert more casual viewers into more active consumers of a brand.

Commercial partners that commit across multiple contract cycles can also make a more permanent impression in the minds of a club or sports fanbase, which can better protect a company against short-term performance dips in the off-season.

But for a sports sponsorship to truly resonate with fans, it needs to deliver clear benefits to the local communities and grassroots organisations associated with the sport.

Corporate sponsors are facing growing scrutiny around social responsibility, with Edelman Sport’s “Pushed to the Limit,” report finding that 71% of fans believe that sporting organisations and sponsors are putting money ahead of the needs of both athletes and fans.

Sponsorship strategies that fund grassroots facilities, support gender parity and expand local youth programmes can build measurable goodwill across fanbases – with a sports sponsorship by Wakefield Research finding that brands that fans see as committed to community will see a 71.4% increase in average brand equity.

This localised investment drives deeper engagement, directly supporting overall commercial goals while expanding the broader sporting ecosystem.

While Spain may have won the FIFA World Cup 2026 in the traditional sense, Coca-Cola had a win of its own: research from Kantar found the company had the highest brand lift of any advertiser it measured.

In fact, Henrique Braun, CEO of Coca-Cola, shared in an earnings call that the company had seen more than 80% of purchases at venues across 16 host cities included a Coca-Cola product.

But what made the company’s sponsorship of the World Cup so impactful? Outside of stadium presence, the company’s strategy focused on building localised fan experiences – such as physical fan spaces, AR experiences and commemorative cans – to help make football more interactive for fans.

This turned many passive fans into more active consumers over the course of the tournament, helping to accelerate sales volume.

“This past quarter, we brought to life a unique moment with our globally connected FIFA World Cup campaign,” Manuel Arroyo, EVP, Chief Marketing and Customer Commercial Officer of the Coca-Cola Company, said on LinkedIn.

“It’s been an incredible experience and opportunity to celebrate fans, communities and connections around the world. I’m proud of our global colleagues across the Coca-Cola system for their continued dedication to our business.”

O2 has been sponsoring England Rugby for 30 years – making it the longest standing professional sports shirt sponsorship in the world. But a logo on a shirt is only a small part of this all-encompassing partnership.

In 2021, O2 signed a five-year deal with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) in a commitment to gender parity, making it the first major brand in the sports industry to pledge equal marketing spend and funding across both the Men’s and Women’s teams.

Since then, the company has been focusing on closing the gender awareness gap in rugby. In 2025, O2 and the RFU renewed the agreement with a new five-year partnership deal – including a dedication to investing and improving on the fan experience.

title: Canal+ acquires multi-territory broadcast rights to Icons Cup South Africa
article_text:
Canal+ has acquired the broadcast rights to the first Icons Cup South Africa through a multi-territory agreement with the Icons Series. The partnership puts the cross-sport golf event on SuperSport via DStv. It covers Sub-Saharan Africa, France and select international territories, so the new event has a pay-TV home in its host region and in Canal+’s domestic market. Terms were not disclosed.

SuperSport will show the morning sessions on SuperSport Grandstand and the afternoon sessions on SuperSport Golf. Additional coverage and highlights will run on SuperSport Blitz and DStv CatchUp. The three-day event takes place at The Links at Fancourt in George from 11 to 13 December 2026. Team South Africa, captained by Ernie Els, plays José María Olazábal’s Team World, and the squads include players from rugby, cricket, football, golf, swimming and tennis.

Icons Series chief content officer Chris Sice said the agreement marked a major milestone for the series. “By pairing premium golf coverage with entertainment-led storytelling, mic’d-up access, and high-tempo matchplay, we’re delivering a fast-paced, lean-forward live show,” Sice said.

Rendani Ramovha, Canal+ senior vice president for sports content in English- and Portuguese-speaking Africa, said the company was pleased to bring the tournament to Sub-Saharan African audiences.

The rights deal gives the Icons Cup the second half of its commercial base. Earlier this month, Heineken Beverages signed a two-year partnership that relies partly on broadcast integrations for its Windhoek, Savanna and Amarula activations. With SuperSport now confirmed, those integrations have a channel and a pay-TV audience across the region.

SuperSport already carries LIV Golf, which held its first South African event in Johannesburg in March. The Icons Cup is a different product. It is sold on Springbok and Proteas names rather than tour professionals, so it can reach viewers who would watch AB de Villiers putt before they would watch a regular tour event. The three-day format and in-house production also make it straightforward to programme across two channels in December.

Since completing its takeover of MultiChoice in 2025, Canal+ can buy content once and use it in both its African and French markets. Here it gets an event staged in South Africa that also has international names for its home audience.

The Icons Series has now signed both a headline sponsor and a broadcaster before its African debut has been played. Heineken’s deal runs for two years, but the length of the broadcast agreement was not disclosed.

title: Siniakova, Townsend seal semifinal berth; Errani, Paolini stay unbeaten at FAGE WTA Finals

title: Eugenio Chacarra still likes his chances as he targets Race to Dubai title
article_text:
Eugenio Chacarra said if he can clean up his card over the weekend he likes his chances to win both the DP World Tour Championship and the Race to Dubai crown following a one under par 71 on the second day at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

The Race to Dubai leader made back-to-back birdies to finish a rollercoaster day in Dubai, adding a second round 71 to an opening 72 that sees him hold a share of 11th after 36 holes on one-under.

The Spaniard, who is the only three-time winner on the DP World Tour this season, has plenty of experience making the most of the weekend and said he was happy with his finish as he looks to make the most of his opportunity to become the third Spaniard in history to win the Race to Dubai.

"I like how I'm hitting it," Chacarra said. "Like you said, there's been a lot of birdies in harder conditions. So if I can clean up the card a little, I like my chance on the weekend.

"It's obviously playing tough. That's been kind of the thing the last two weeks, my good's good, but I'm making too many mistakes and I'm not being able to get the momentum going.

"I made a bomb on the par-3 13, and I hit a good driver on 14, kind of like getting momentum, and I hit the worst shot of the week from nowhere.

"It's kind of been the week. I still have two days. I'm happy with that finish I needed. Only six back. Hopefully Rory can have that good of a back nine, and I still have a chance to win the tournament.

Eugenio Chacarra with a birdie-birdie finish to head into the weekend at -1 👏#DPWTC | #RolexSeries pic.twitter.com/m2YL5SJFah

Chacarra made the perfect start to his round with back-to-back birdies before dropping a shot at the fourth, making the turn in one under following a birdie-bogey end to his front nine. A second consecutive bogey at the tenth brought him back to level par, and although he responded with a birdie at the 13th, further dropped shots at the 14th and 15th left him needing a strong finish, which he duly delivered with back-to-back birdies.

With nearest challenger Rory McIlroy four ahead and in a share of the lead, Chacarra is currently projected to finish second on the Race to Dubai, but said it was a challenge that he expected to face this week.

Yet he is also aware there is plenty more golf to play, and is ready to attempt the challenge.

"I mean, it's just what it is. I knew it was going to happen. It's one of the favourite courses of Rory and he's had so much success in here. He's obviously one of the best players in the world.

"So we know it's going to be tough. Like I said, there's two rounds of golf, 36 holes is a lot. I can control what I can control. If Rory comes here and wins the tournament, he's a deserved champion. There's nothing I can really do.

I'm going to try to win the tournament. As of right now, I'm six shots back. The wind is kind of pumping. It's not easy out there.

"So, like I said, hopefully they don't go really, really low. And, I mean, six shots on a weekend, it's not a lot."

title: England Netball launches ‘Built by Women’ campaign
article_text:
England Netball has launched Built by Women, a new campaign celebrating the people, history and community behind the sport as it seeks to unlock greater investment.

Created by Brothers & Sisters, the campaign positions netball as a sport with a unique cultural and commercial proposition: built by women, for women, and powered by one of the largest participation bases in UK sport.

At its centre is a 72-second film in which women come together to construct a giant netball player from the ground up. She rises to 100 feet, reflecting 100 years of England Netball.

The film is set in Manchester and looks ahead to the Netball World Cup 2031, which will be held at Co-op Live following England Netball’s successful bid to host the tournament. It will be the fourth time England has hosted the event.

Fran Connolly, CEO of England Netball, said, “Netball has always been built by women, for women. It is a sport where women and girls can compete fiercely, lead confidently and take up space on their own terms.“

“Built by Women is about celebrating that heritage and using it to shape the next chapter for our sport. We want more people to see the energy, community and opportunity within netball and how our sport connects so deeply with women and girls across the country.”

The launch comes as England Netball and its Chair, Baroness Sue Campbell, join organisations across sport in supporting The Equal Sport Project. Launched on 10th November, the cross-sector initiative aims to make the UK the world’s leading nation for women and girls’ sport by removing the barriers to participating, competing, leading and succeeding.

Baroness Sue Campbell, Chair of England Netball, said, “Women’s sport has reached a defining moment. We have seen extraordinary progress over the past decade, but we know that equality will not happen by accident. It requires leadership, ambition and a willingness to redesign the system so that women and girls are considered from the very beginning, not as an afterthought.“

“The Equal Sport Project is about more than recognising the challenge; it is about committing to action together. If we get this right, the UK can become the best place in the world for every woman and girl to play, compete, coach, lead and thrive in sport.”

title: All Blacks aim to eliminate threat of Wales flanker Morgan
article_text:
New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie says they have spoken about eliminating the breakdown threat of Wales flanker Jac Morgan in the Nations Championship match in Cardiff on Saturday.

The All Blacks are firm favourites to extend their 73-year winning run against Wales this weekend.

But New Zealand have identified Morgan’s contact area work as one of Wales’ main strengths.

"When [Wales] chop tackle, you've got guys like Morgan who are excellent on the ball," said Rennie.

"So we're well aware of that and we'll have a focus on eliminating him before he can cause us stress, because that is a big part of their game."

Rennie highlighted other issues that concern him about Wales.

"Their line-out has been excellent during the last year," he said, even though Steve Tandy's side saw six of their throws go astray last weekend.

"Maybe it was not quite as accurate against Japan but up until then, it's been top-notch," the veteran coach added.

"They're also prepared to play and, in Tomos Williams, they have one of the best nines in the world.

"We've got to make sure we don't let him have too much space, because he's got such a high-quality kicking game and kicks off both feet.

"They've got a number of players that if we give them time and space, they'll be a handful.

"They have a big midfield and absolute jets on the wing, so we know a fair bit about the enemy."

Rennie has made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland 43-21.

Sections of the New Zealand media say that selection reflects the lack of threat Wales pose, as the 10th-ranked side in the world face the second, but Rennie does not subscribe to that view.

"Wales will be pretty fired up to put in a quality performance," he said.

"So we've picked a strong side we think will show the respect for them."

Rennie is also familiar with many of the Wales coaching staff.

He was Glasgow coach between 2017 and 2020 when Wales duo Tandy and Danny Wilson were part of Gregor Townsend's Scotland backroom staff.

Wales defence coach Peter Murchie was also part of Rennie's backroom team at Kobelco Kobe Steelers in Japan before linking up with Tandy in the Welsh set-up.

"I know them well and they are very good, smart coaches," said Rennie.

"Pete did a phenomenal job defensively with us at Kobe, and I can see the impact he's having already. And likewise with Steve.

"It's going to take time to turn things around, but I can definitely see the impact they're having."

Rennie has bittersweet memories of coaching an international side against Wales at the Principality Stadium, when he was leading Australia in December 2022.

He masterminded a wonderful Wallabies comeback as Wales led 34-13 before the tourists scored 26 unanswered points to win 39-34.

It proved to be Rennie's final action as Australia coach. He was replaced by Eddie Jones, while the Wales boss that day, Wayne Pivac, was dismissed with Warren Gatland returning.

Rennie remembers the atmosphere that day.

"It is one of the great grounds in world rugby, with the roof on, the national anthems you've got to soak it up and enjoy it," he said.

"It can be pretty daunting, but it's special.

"We'll definitely embrace that and all the boys are excited to be here."

Listen live on BBC Radio Wales, BBC Radio Cymru and BBC Radio 5Live.

New Zealand have won the past 34 Tests against Wales in a winning sequence that stretches back to 1953, with the All Blacks scoring more than 50 points on each of their three previous visits to Cardiff over the past five years.

New Zealand and South Africa are currently unbeaten in the southern hemisphere table, competing for top spot before the Nations Championship play-off weekend at the end of the month.

Rennie, however, says his side are not concentrating on trying to close the points-difference gap on the Springboks.

"It's just a Test match and our focus is this week," he insisted.

"We'll probably be looking at things going into the last game, where it might be a little bit clearer around what we need to do.

"I think South Africa are about 70 points clear, so if we end up on the same amount of points, it's unlikely we'd catch them.

"There's a real danger to go out and think you need to score X amount of points, you end up overplaying and getting embarrassed.

"We've got a clear plan around how we want to play and whatever happens, happens."

title: Scotland freshen up back three for Australia clash as Wallabies boosted by Carter Gordon return

title: Coco Gauff explains what she really meant when she called the the WTA Finals ‘stupid’
article_text:
Coco Gauff made headlines when she brandished the WTA Finals as ‘kinda stupid’ after her defeat to Linda Noskova.

“The scenarios, I know they make sense, but they’re kinda stupid. If I win my match [Thursday] and I still don’t qualify, I’m like, ‘It’s okay, it’s cool.’ I’m looking forward to next year. I can’t say much, but everybody knows that has to change,” said Gauff.

Gauff did win her final match at the WTA Finals, against Marta Kostyuk, but she didn’t qualify for the semifinals, missing out to Jessica Pegula.

After confirmation that she would no longer play a part in the 2026 WTA Finals, she clarified what she meant when she called the format ‘stupid’.

In an interview with The Tennis Channel after beating Kostyuk, Gauff said: “I wasn’t saying the format was stupid. I was saying if you get in your head while you’re playing into all the scenarios, that’s stupid.”

Gauff’s comments suggested there could be a major overhaul of the WTA Finals format and she also divulged what she has heard about that.

“Did I leak info that’s kind of already out there?,” said Gauff. “Sue me, I don’t know.”

It is currently unclear what format change for the WTA Finals would be, but it would be very disappointing to see the tournament revert to a straight knockout.

The WTA Finals’ round robin phase is a nice change from the knockout format players compete in for the other 10 months of the year.

It could water down the format of the WTA Finals at the end of a gruelling season and make it less special for the top players to compete in.

Prior to 2002, the WTA Finals was a straight knockout tournament for the top 16 players on the WTA Tour.

It’s hard to see that being interesting enough to sustain tennis fans in a world where they essentially get to see that at every tournament across the entire calendar in women’s tennis.

Introducing another eight players would also not make the tournament any more star-studded either, outside of potentially Alexandra Eala’s involvement in the event.

The likes of Elise Mertens, Sorana Cirstea, and Maja Chwalinska, who currently occupy positions between world No 8 and world No 16, would not be putting any more bums on seats when it came to television ratings or ticket sales.

Nevertheless, it looks like a major change is incoming for the WTA Finals and Gauff has all but confirmed the news following her exit from this year’s tournament.

title: Uganda: African crown opens door to SVNS 3 · SNA
article_text:
Uganda won more than a final in Nairobi: the Lady Cranes secured their place in HSBC SVNS 3 by beating Tunisia 33 to 0 on 8 November at the RFUEA Grounds. This first Africa Women’s Sevens title opens up a stage on the international women’s rugby sevens pathway.

The scoreline in the final underlined their dominance. Yet it does not tell the story of the toughest passage in their tournament: a few hours earlier, against Kenya, the Ugandans were still behind when the final siren sounded.

- Uganda win the African final 33 to 0 against Tunisia.

- A 19 to 14 victory over Kenya, snatched with the final play, had sent them into the final.

- The Lady Cranes qualify for HSBC SVNS 3.

In the semi-final, Uganda had opened up a twelve-point lead before seeing the Kenyans turn the score around. The hosts led 14 to 12 and had the ball when the siren sounded. The possession still had to be completed: time running out is not enough, on its own, to bring a rugby sevens match to an immediate halt.

The Lady Cranes kept the move alive until their captain Peace Lekuru went over for the decisive try. The 19 to 14 win allowed them to stay in the competition. Having already scored a first try in that semi-final, Lekuru later received the player of the tournament award.

The final brought a different scenario. Lydia Namabiro scored three tries, while Racheal Mufuwa and Gertrude Kateesa also crossed. Five tries in all took Uganda to 33 points, without Tunisia managing to reply with a single one.

The Tunisians had booked their place in the final by beating Zimbabwe 22 to 10. They leave Nairobi in second place, while Kenya won the bronze-medal match against the Zimbabweans, 27 to 7. The podium brings together two East African sides, Uganda and Kenya, and one North African side, Tunisia.

Uganda’s run cannot be reduced to the final two matches. In the pool stage, the Lady Cranes had beaten Burkina Faso, Mauritius and Madagascar without conceding a point. Their defence was then tested more in the quarter-final, won 24 to 17 against South Africa A.

Those six wins, from the pools to the final, give clear substance to the qualification: Uganda won their three knockout matches after an unbeaten first day. The ticket to SVNS 3 is secured. It is the Lady Cranes’ next sporting step after their title on 8 November in Nairobi.

title: Dakar 2026 YOG: Kenya gold, Madagascar bronze in rugby sevens
article_text:
Kenya have been named women’s rugby sevens champions at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games after beating Australia 17-12 in the final after extra time. Madagascar are listed as bronze medallists, with a 26-10 win over Czechia.

In the final, Darci Mackay opened the scoring for Australia. Kenya captain Zain Hido brought the two sides level at 5-5 by half-time. Grace Buchanan then scored, Billie Backus added the conversion, and Australia led 12-5. Late on, Josphine Kerubo scored a try for Kenya, converted by Diana Wanjiku. Mitchelle Chemtai scored the decisive try two minutes after the start of extra time.

Kenya’s run also included a 12-5 win over China, a 19-0 victory against Senegal, a 17-5 defeat by Australia in the pool stage and a 15-5 semi-final win over Madagascar. The title is also described as the first gold for an African team in rugby sevens at the Olympic Games or the YOG, Kenya’s first medal at Dakar 2026 and Kenya’s first Olympic title in a team sport. Madagascar’s bronze is presented as a first medal at the Olympic Games or the Youth Olympic Games for Madagascar.

The Kenyan team was made up of 16 and 17-year-old students. The squad went into camp in the second week of September, under the guidance of Knight Otuoma and an all-female technical staff.

title: Former PGA Tour pro admits LIV Golf move may have been a mistake
article_text:
Ben An has revealed his decision to quit the PGA Tour for LIV Golf may not have been the best choice.

The South Korean joined the breakaway tour in January 2026 and was immediately appointed captain of the all-Korean quartet after Kevin Na (pictured) was not offered a new contract.

However, his time with LIV lasted just one season before the league entered bankruptcy and began winding down its operations.

An is not eligible for an immediate return to the PGA Tour, so instead attempted to secure his playing privileges for the 2027 season by entering DP World Tour qualifying school.

It proved a successful week for An, who was among 21 players to earn a card for the 2027 campaign.

Sam Horsfield, Michael La Sasso, Yosuke Asaji, Luis Masaveu and Thomas Pieters were among the LIV contingent who fell short.

An finished tied for eighth at Infinitum in Spain after six rounds of competition, securing his Tour card and avoiding the uncertainty now facing several former LIV players.

He has previously enjoyed considerable success on the DP World Tour, winning twice, including the prestigious BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth in 2015.

The former PGA Tour player had remained largely silent on social media during the uncertainty surrounding LIV's future, explaining that he wanted to avoid speculation while considering his next move.

In a post on X, An said he had not regretted his decision to play in LIV Golf but acknowledged that, with hindsight, it may not have been the right career move.

"It may not be the best decision looking back but I enjoyed every moment while I was playing in the league," he wrote.

"Holding onto the past and worrying about the future are two of the harmful things you can do to yourself. One door closed with LIV but another has opened.

"I'm looking forward play 2027 season in DP World Tour again."

An's comments come as former LIV Golf players face an uncertain period following the league's financial collapse, with questions remaining over where several of its leading names will compete next.

The biggest question mark surrounds Bryson DeChambeau.

The two-time US Open champion recently broke his silence on LIV's collapse, insisting he did everything he could to save the league.

However, he stopped short of revealing what he intends to do next season.

DeChambeau has been offered the chance to play on the DP World Tour in 2027, but he has until 15 November to accept the offer.

Former European Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley warned DeChambeau that turning it down and concentrating on YouTube golf would be "a dumb move".

"The longer Bryson stays away and off traditional platforms, the less chance he has of winning major championships going forward, because you cut your teeth in week-to-week PGA and DP World Tour events before you elevate into these major championships.

"And if you're cutting your teeth playing fun golf and LIV golf, it's a massive step up to then try and compete at the very, very top against the best players in the world. It's just not going to happen. It's not going to happen.

"You're training and preparation to win major championships at such a low level that you cannot step up in that way.

"So if he does it, I think it would pretty much close the door on winning major championships during that period of time."

title: NHL’s next media deal will test the league’s strength
article_text:
One of the biggest developing stories in entertainment and sports is how the world's biggest media companies judge the value of non-NFL rights. The NHL will be the first public test into this new era of media valuation.

The NHL can begin formally negotiating a new media rights deal with its incumbent partners — Disney/ESPN and Skydance, the new owner of TNT Sports — on Jan. 1. The league wants an increase in overall rights fees between 50% and 100% over its current deal, according to sources familiar with the matter. The NHL inked a 7-year, $4.5 billion deal with ESPN and TNT Sports in 2021.

Whether the league actually gets that type of increase is still unclear — and that will be one of the most watched data points in the world of sports business next year.

National media rights for the NHL currently make up about 13% of its annual revenue, which is around $8 billion, according to CNBC estimates.

Disney/ESPN and Skydance want to renew a deal with the league, according to people familiar with the matter that asked not to be named because the discussions are private. Both companies have engaged in preliminary conversations with the league in the past few weeks, and while there's still work to do in terms of price, there's mutual interest in getting something done.

In its current deal, ESPN has access to 100 exclusive games for the 2026-27 season. Fifty-three of them air on ESPN or ABC, and the other 47 exclusive stream on ESPN. Under current terms, the league's playoffs are split between Disney and TNT Sports.

Disney is particularly interested in acquiring the rights to more playoff games, one of the people said. The NHL had its most-watched playoffs on record last season, averaging 1.8 million viewers per game. The Stanley Cup averaged 5.2 million viewers — the largest audience since 2019. It was played between the Carolina Hurricanes and the Vegas Golden Knights — not exactly marquee NHL franchises.

Last year's regular season averaged 546,000 viewers across ESPN/ABC and TNT Sports, up 25% from a year ago — the highest average in more than a decade.

The sport is also having a moment culturally. Earlier this year, HBO Max said its hockey-romance series "Heated Rivalry" averaged a whopping 10.6 million viewers per episode.

International hockey competitions, such as the league's annual "4 Nations Face-Off" midseason tournament and the 2026 Winter Olympics, have drawn huge ratings. The last "4 Nations Face-Off" game — 2025's U.S. vs. Canada final — drew 9.3 million viewers.

This year's Gold Medal men's hockey game between the U.S. and Canada averaged a stunning 26 million viewers on NBC and Peacock in the U.S., according to Nielsen data. That made it the most-watched sporting event in U.S. history with a start time before 9 a.m. ET.

"We think we've got the best content," NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said on CNBC last month. "Our ratings have continued to increase. We were up dramatically into the double digits last year. So we view ourselves coming into the marketplace in a very strong position. Having said that, the marketplace is extremely competitive and extremely fragmented. But, I believe that with fierce competition that's going on between traditional television and the newer media platforms that there'll be a great opportunity for us to both expand our reach and get paid what we think is an appropriate reflection of our value."

Recent history suggests the NHL will get the rights increase it wants. The NBA nearly tripled its national media rights revenue, signing an 11-year, $77 billion contract with Disney, Amazon and NBCUniversal in a deal that started last season.

The NHL also renewed its TV rights deal in Canada just last year with Rogers Communications, scoring an increase of more than 100% annually when adjusting for currency fluctuations.

But recent history may not match up to present reality.

While Skydance is interested in getting a deal done, the company's top priorities are paying down debt and saving money to pay for what's going to be a huge NFL rights increase — potentially $1 billion per season or more, two of the people said.

Skydance is dead set on renewing the NFL, said one of the people. Those talks will likely occur in 2028, as the league has an opt-out clause at the end of the 2029-30 season.

The NHL was a meaningful sports property to Warner Bros. Discovery. The company could use its loyal fanbase and sizable playoff ratings to help justify distribution fees to pay TV providers while marginally adding some subscribers to HBO Max.

Now that Paramount and WBD have been pushed together, the NHL isn't as important to Skydance for distribution leverage, which already has premier sports media rights such as the NFL, The Masters, college football, March Madness, UFC and UEFA Champions League.

That's not to say the NHL isn't a priority for Skydance. Skydance still needs programming for the cable networks it owns to keep that business chugging along. But relative to WBD, it's not as much of a must-have.

"As it relates to future rights, we'll be disciplined," Skydance CEO David Ellison said during an earnings conference call this week — perhaps hinting at his company dropping not only NHL but also other rights from the WBD portfolio in the coming months and years. "Every right has to earn its place."

Perhaps Skydance remains a partner but buys fewer NHL games or sublicenses some of them. This potentially opens the door to new bidders. CNBC's own parent company Versant would be interested in a slice of NHL games. Amazon sniffs around just about every national sports property that comes to market.

title: Australia make three changes for Scotland clash as Rob Valetini returns
article_text:
Australia have made three changes to their starting XV for Sunday’s clash with Scotland at Murrayfield as Rob Valetini, Carter Gordon and Harry Potter return to the side.

Valetini has been restored at blindside flanker following the Wallabies’ defeat to England, reuniting with Fraser McReight and captain Harry Wilson in the back row.

Gordon will make his return from a fractured fibula at fly-half and partners Ryan Lonergan in the half-backs, while Potter has been selected on the wing alongside Max Jorgensen and Tom Wright in the back three.

The Edinburgh encounter will hold particular significance for Potter, who returns to the venue where he made his Test debut.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii moves back into midfield following an injury to Isaac Henry and will partner Len Ikitau for the 18th time at Test level.

There is also a positional switch for Western Force captain Jeremy Williams, who moves back into the second row alongside Josh Canham.

The front row of Angus Bell, Billy Pollard and Allan Alaalatoa remains unchanged, with the latter set to win his 98th Wallabies cap as he closes in on becoming Australia's 14th Test centurion.

Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Lachlan Shaw and Tom Hooper are the three changes among the replacements. Shaw is in line for his first Test appearance in Europe, while Hooper returns after recovering from a shoulder injury.

Tate McDermott, Ben Donaldson and Filipo Daugunu retain their places among the replacement backs.

The Wallabies head into the match sitting third in the Nations Championship Southern Hemisphere standings, with head coach Les Kiss demanding a response following their loss to England.

"We’ve had a good week of training but after falling short of our own expectations last week it’s vital we transfer our hard work onto the field for the 80 minutes on Sunday," Kiss said.

"Playing Scotland on their home turf is a massive Test and we're all determined to make our supporters proud by elevating our game to the level it needs to be."

Wallabies team: Tom Wright; Max Jorgensen, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii, Len Ikitau, Harry Potter; Carter Gordon, Ryan Lonergan; Angus Bell, Billy Pollard, Allan Alaalatoa; Jeremy Williams, Josh Canham; Rob Valetini, Fraser McReight, Harry Wilson (capt).

Replacements: Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Isaac Kailea, Taniela Tupou, Lachlan Shaw, Tom Hooper, Tate McDermott, Ben Donaldson, Filipo Daugunu.

title: Adam Jones named Harlequins head coach for two games
article_text:
Former Wales and British & Irish Lions prop Adam Jones is set to take charge of Harlequins for their next two PREM Rugby Cup fixtures.

The 45-year-old will assume temporary head coach duties for the matches against Newcastle Red Bulls and Saracens.

The announcement comes despite Australian Jason Gilmore already holding the permanent head coach position at the London club.

Jones, who won 95 caps for Wales, has spent several years building his reputation as one of rugby's leading scrum coaches.

Now he gets the chance to call the shots himself.

According to a Harlequins statement shared by RugbyInsideLine, Jones will assume head coach duties for the club's two upcoming PREM Rugby Cup fixtures.

His first assignment comes against Newcastle Red Bulls at Kingston Park on Saturday, 14 November.

The decision has attracted attention because Jason Gilmore remains the club's permanent head coach.

There is no suggestion that Jones's appointment represents a permanent change at The Stoop.

The temporary promotion comes just weeks after Jones committed his future to Harlequins.

In September, the club announced a new contract for the former Wales international, confirming he would continue as scrum and contact coach.

Jones originally joined Quins as a player in 2015 before moving into coaching three years later.

He was part of the coaching setup when Harlequins lifted the English Premiership title in 2021.

The former Ospreys prop also helped Wales win three Six Nations Grand Slams and toured twice with the British & Irish Lions.

He gained further international coaching experience with Wales in 2025.

His latest assignment offers another opportunity to develop his coaching credentials.

Whether it opens the door to a permanent head coaching position elsewhere remains to be seen.
