title: WOWOW becomes exclusive home of WTA Tour in Japan through 2030
article_text:
LONDON and TOKYO -- WTA Ventures and WOWOW have announced a new four-year media rights agreement that will see WOWOW become the exclusive home of the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in Japan from 2027 through 2030.

The agreement will give Japanese audiences access to the world’s leading tennis players throughout the season, with WOWOW holding exclusive rights to WTA 1000, WTA 500 and WTA 250 tournaments, as well as the prestigious season-ending WTA Finals.

The partnership marks the return of comprehensive, year-round WTA Tour coverage to Japan, reconnecting audiences with elite women’s tennis and creating a platform to build the profile of the sport in one of tennis’ most established markets.

Japan has a rich history in women’s tennis and continues to be represented at the highest level, led by four-time Grand Slam champion, former World No. 1 and current World No. 17 Naomi Osaka. Japanese audiences will be able to follow Osaka and the next generation of homegrown talent alongside global stars including Aryna Sabalenka, Coco Gauff, Iga Swiatek and Elena Rybakina as they compete across the season.

Ahead of the four-year agreement beginning in 2027, WOWOW will also exclusively broadcast the 2026 WTA Finals in Japan under a separate agreement with DAZN.

Taking place at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in California from November 8-15, the WTA Finals brings together the season’s top eight singles players and doubles teams as they compete for the prestigious year-end titles.

"Japan has a proud tennis heritage and has produced some of the most recognizable and successful players in our sport, so we are delighted to partner with WOWOW to establish a new long-term home for the WTA in the market," said WTA Ventures CEO Marina Storti.

"WOWOW has an outstanding track record in tennis and shares our ambition to showcase the personalities, rivalries and world-class competition that make the WTA so compelling. This long-term partnership gives us an important platform to reconnect with existing tennis fans, reach new audiences and build greater visibility and value for women’s tennis in Japan.”

Already home to all four Grand Slam tournaments in Japan, WOWOW has a longstanding association with tennis and will further expand its offering with year-round WTA Tour coverage from 2027.

title: Shorts: Runna, Leicester Tigers, MSQ Sport + Entertainment
article_text:
London-based running app Runna has become the training partner of the Barcelona Marathon, Barcelona Half Marathon and San Sebastián Marathon, in a deal with race organiser RPM Sports.

The app, owned by Strava, will provide personalised training plans and coaching for runners preparing for the three Spanish races. Runners who sign up for any of the events will receive two weeks of Runna free.

The agreement gives Runna a presence at some of Europe’s largest mass participation races, with a strong international field. The Zurich Marató Barcelona sold a record 27,000 places in 2025, 60% of them to international runners from 109 countries, and passed 30,000 registered runners for its 2026 edition. RPM Sports also organises the eDreams Mitja Marató Barcelona and the Zurich Maratón San Sebastián.

Runna was founded in London in 2021 by Dom Maskell and Ben Parker and launched publicly in March 2022. Strava, which is based in San Francisco, bought the business in April 2025. It has since run Runna as a separate app, with teams in London and Boston.

The Barcelona Marathon has also become one of the fastest courses in the world. In March, Ethiopia’s Fotyen Tesfay won the women’s race in 2:10:51, the second-fastest women’s marathon time ever recorded

Leicester Tigers have partnered with Carlsberg Britvic, the UK’s largest multi-beverage supplier, making Pepsi the soft drink partner of the Gallagher PREM club.

Pepsi MAX is the flagship product across Mattioli Woods Welford Road, with Tango and 7UP also on sale around the ground.

Carlsberg Britvic has also supported the installation of modern pouring technology at the stadium. The equipment is designed to give supporters a consistently high-quality drink on every matchday visit.

Formed in January 2025, Carlsberg Britvic brought together Carlsberg Marston’s and Hemel Hempstead-based Britvic following Carlsberg’s £3.3bn takeover. Its portfolio includes Robinsons, Tango and J2O. Under exclusive PepsiCo agreements, the business makes, markets and sells Pepsi MAX, 7UP, Lipton Ice Tea and Rockstar Energy. In 2025, Britvic secured its first 20-year bottling arrangement with PepsiCo in Great Britain.

The soft drinks business has become a key growth driver for its Danish parent. Carlsberg reported that soft drink volumes rose 7.8% in the first half of 2026, largely thanks to Britvic, with integration savings arriving faster than expected.

The partnership completes a refreshed drinks line-up at Welford Road. BrewDog began a five-year beer partnership with Tigers from the start of the 2026-27 season, while Thatchers holds exclusive cider pouring rights at the stadium.

It also adds to a busy commercial period for the club. Halo Cantera holds the front-of-shirt position on the men’s kit for 2026-27, Pharmacy2U and Wayfair joined on multi-year deals from this season, and Heath Lodge Clinic became medical partner on 2nd November.

Former Anheuser-Busch and Cirkul marketing executive Michael Goon has joined MSQ Sport + Entertainment as Executive Vice President in North America.

Goon moves to the agency after several years leading marketing on the brand side. His experience covers brand strategy, integrated marketing and communications. At Anheuser-Busch he worked on communications for the Better World team, the brewer’s corporate social responsibility platform. He has already been working with the North American team for several weeks.

The appointment adds to the senior leadership of the agency’s North American business, which opened in New York in March 2025. It is led by Chief Executive Officer Steph Lund and Managing Partners Andrea Nirsimloo and Paul Anastasiadis, all former M&C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment executives. The agency added three senior hires in February, including Lauren Weil as Executive Vice President to lead its influencer division. Its North American clients include BODYARMOR and The Hidden Opponent, a non-profit focused on athlete mental health.

MSQ Sport + Entertainment was founded in the UK in June 2024 by Steve Martin and Jamie Wynne-Morgan, who built M&C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment over 20 years. It is part of London-based marketing group MSQ, and Callaway Golf was its founding client.

Michael Goon, Executive Vice President at MSQ Sport + Entertainment, said, “After spending the past several years leading marketing for brands, I’m excited to bring that experience back to the agency side—partnering with talented teams and clients to build impactful, integrated marketing programs.“

“I’ve already had the opportunity to collaborate with the MSQ team over the past few weeks and am energized by what’s ahead!”

Leeds Rhinos Foundation has joined forces with Westward Care in a partnership designed to bring generations together and support healthy ageing for older people across Leeds.

The partnership with one of the city’s leading care providers for older people launched at AMT Headingley Stadium on 12th November. Senior managers and colleagues from across Westward Care attended to help shape the programme.

The partnership is built around shared values and links the community spirit of rugby league with Westward Care’s commitment to helping older people live well. It also carries the provider’s LOVE values of trust, kindness, respect and teamwork into new activities and relationships.

Plans for the year ahead include sporting memories and rugby heritage sessions, chances for residents to meet younger players and local clubs, and projects focused on movement, mobility, wellbeing and nutrition. The programme will develop around residents’ interests, with opportunities to recognise and celebrate Westward Care colleagues.

Peter Hodkinson, Managing Director of Westward Care, said, “Rugby league has a special place in the life of Leeds, and many of our residents have their own memories and connections with the sport. This partnership gives us a wonderful opportunity to build on those connections and create new ones.“

title: 'There's no guarantees': Dave Rennie on overlooked All Blacks trio
article_text:
With Chay Fihaki, Josh Jacomb, and Saula Ma’u waiting in the wings for their chance on the All Blacks‘ Nations Championship Northern Tour, head coach Dave Rennie explained the challenge facing the trio as they wait for an opportunity in the remaining two Tests of 2026.

Many believed the Nations Championship contest against Wales was a chance to give Josh Jacomb a first Test start, while Fihaki and Ma’u remain as depth options heading into the final two weeks of the four-Test tour.

Jacomb started for the All Blacks in their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry midweek match against the Bulls in Pretoria, and featured off the bench against both the Lions and the Sharks.

The new Highlanders recruit currently sits behind Ruben Love, Damian McKenzie, and Richie Mo’unga in the pecking order, while experienced veteran Beauden Barrett is also an option in the No.10 jersey.

For Ma’u, he had one appearance off the bench in the All Blacks’ 41-35 victory over the Lions in Johannesburg, but is stuck behind both Fletcher Newell and Pasilio Tosi on the end-of-year tour.

Fihaki, who made his Test debut off the bench at Sydney’s Accor Stadium in the 2026 Bledisloe Cup Test match against Australia, could come into the selection picture against England with Will Jordan nursing a hamstring tear, but seems unlikely.

When asked about why the trio didn’t feature in the 23-man squad for the Wales Test match in Cardiff, Rennie outlined his reasoning.

“There are no guarantees. We talk a lot about earning the right to play, and all three of the guys who missed out in selection in the first two weeks have all played in the jersey before,” Rennie said in Cardiff.

“Obviously, Chay got a Test debut in Sydney, and the other two boys played in Africa. So, doesn’t mean that they won’t get an opportunity on this tour. But yeah, based on, you know, obviously Richie coming back, that made sense.

“Some, you know, we were keen to have, obviously, Beauden in the mix as well, and he can cover 10 so look, certainly the three boys who haven’t stripped yet are determined, and their jobs to continue to train well and apply pressure.

“We just decided in the end it will give us a little bit more experience. I mean, if we got under pressure with so many guys lacking experience, it could put us under a bit of pressure.

“We want to pay respect to Wales too. We‘ve picked a side that we think will show some respect for them.”

Rennie provided an update on the fitness of Jordan, who is touch and go for the Nations Championship finals weekend after picking up a minor “hamstring tear” against Scotland.

“Yeah, no, he’s a chance to be available in the last week,” the All Blacks coach said.

“He’s got boxes to tick along the way, so he’s been doing a little bit of strength work over the last couple of days, and the plan is to run him Saturday, I think.

“And if he has any setbacks amongst that, then he’s likely to return home. But at this stage, he’s a chance to play in that final week, so he’ll remain in camp.”

title: England respond to 'rugby genius' Eddie Jones' threat of left-field tactics
article_text:
England have hit back at Eddie Jones’ claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming clash with New Zealand.

Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick’s side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be “a little bit distracted” by the All Blacks’ visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21.

New Zealand are the box office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan.

“That’s nowhere near the case because we understand how important this game is,” scrum coach Tom Harrison said.

“We understand the challenge Japan can throw at us and we have to be alive in every single moment to the type of rugby they play.

“We understand that there might be unorthodox things coming our way, but our need is to be alive.

“I’ve never worked with Eddie but I’ve met him a few times and he’s a rugby genius, the way he thinks about the game and the way the players talk about him.”

Cadan Murley wins his eighth cap but first at Twickenham after coming in for the injured Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the left wing as one of 10 changes made for Japan.

Murley, Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph are aiming to make an impression on Borthwick after the head coach signalled that places in next year’s World Cup squad are up for grabs.

“I just want go out there and play my best rugby,” Murley said. “I’ll focus on what I can do, control the controllables, and hopefully that will get me in the mix further down the line.

“But my sole focus is on this game and putting my best foot forward. It’s my first game at Twickenham and that’s what’s on my mind at the moment.”

title: Legends to help Georgia Rugby celebrate historic occasion in Tbilisi
article_text:
Five members of the original Georgian men’s national team will be present at the Avchala Stadium in Tbilisi on Saturday to witness the Lelos’ 300th international match.

In a way it is fitting that Tonga are the opponents this weekend because one of the team’s proudest days was when they beat the Ikale ‘Tahi at Rugby World Cup 2015.

Aged 18, and 340 days old, Vasil Lobzhanidze became the youngest-ever player to play in the tournament in that match in Gloucester and he starts Saturday’s encounter at number nine.

Lobzhanidze and none of his teammates were born when the Lelos, initially known as the Shevardens (Falcons), first took to the field.

Representing independent Georgia, the team played its first match back in the Soviet era, on 12 September 1989, beating Zimbabwe 16-3 in Kutaisi.

Since then, the team has continued to make steady progress. Of the 299 matches played so far, the Lelos have recorded 187 victories, 10 draws and 102 defeats. Of those matches, 124 were played in Georgia, 118 away from home and 57 at neutral venues.

In 2003, the Lelos made their Rugby World Cup debut and they have since become regular participants in the tournament and will compete at the world’s premier rugby event for the seventh time next year in Australia.

The dominant force in European rugby outside of the Six Nations, Georgia are currently 13th in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings, having briefly touched 11th in the past.

Of the original 18-man squad, wingers Bartlome Khamashuridze and Aleksander Khvedelidze, centre Malkhaz Cheishvili, No.8 David Ghudushauri and replacement Gela Pirtskhalava will be present in person at the Avchala Stadium to cheer on the modern-day Lelos.

Given the Lelos haven’t lost to Tonga in the four meetings since that RWC 2015 clash and are unbeaten in their first four Nations Cup clashes, the form book suggests they’ll celebrate the occasion with a win.

title: Why England’s fringe figures face World Cup audition against Japan
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

When Eddie Jones was Steve Borthwick’s boss as England head coach, the vastly-experienced Australian explained to his assistant the concept of international rugby’s twin horizons. There is, always, the game immediately ahead, the importance of which must always be underlined to the squad. And then there is the second horizon of every cyclical sport: the World Cup, always occupying the plotting parts of a coaching staff’s minds.

It is that second horizon that has come more sharply into focus ahead of this game against Japan. Borthwick is always conscious of not getting too far ahead of himself, but, having made 10 changes and two more positional tweaks to his starting side from the win over Australia, spoke openly of the opportunity he had presented to some players. Of consideration, too, were the heavy workloads or recent injury returns for a Tommy Freeman or Fin Baxter – and that’s before even mentioning the injuries to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, George Furbank, Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson, even it is hoped that the latter trio will be fit for New Zealand next week.

Amid such upheaval, change can present an ideal chance to look at a few fringe figures. Borthwick believes he knows between 26 and 28 of his likely squad for next year’s tournament – injury and incident permitting, of course. In many ways, then, this is an audition for those final five to seven spots. A need for individuals not to chase individual performance at the expense of that of the collective has been underlined by both assistant coach Kevin Sinfield and George Ford, who returns in place of a rested Fin Smith at fly half, this week.

“The more and the better we play as a team, the better you'll see of people individually,” Ford explained. “We're going like the other way, really. Let's do things together. Let's make sure we're on the same page. Let's do the unseen stuff. And off the back of that, you're going to get some brilliant individual moments in the game, rather than the other way round. Because if you go the other way round, it could end up being clunky and a little bit frustrating, so we don't want to go down that route.”

There are eerie echoes to another encounter against Japan when that balance was not expertly struck. A stuttering 2018 encounter at Twickenham became known as the “black-hole game” – Zach Mercer, Alex Lozowski, Alec Hepburn and Ted Hill are among those seldom sighted since, while Danny Care, substituted at half time, spent four years in exile before clawing his way back in. Ford, in a neat twist, was captain that day. He will surely recall a cautionary tale.

Borthwick’s selection is all the bolder for how it may change how England approach the game. While they retain a lock on the blindside in the ever more influential Alex Coles, the presence of Henry Pollock and Ben Earl in the same starting back row is a rarity. Two volume carriers and explosive athletes could dovetail well; equally, their last outing together came in an Ireland defeat in which England desperately lacked balance. “Henry has had an incredible impact off the bench. And what I want to ensure is that he's bringing that to the start of the game. Both Ben Earl and Henry are great over the ball and what we've got to make sure is that we haven't got all our back-rowers around the ruck. If you have all your back-rowers around the ruck, you're going to get hurt elsewhere.”

The problems of finding the right blend are also evidenced in a new-look backline. How will England adjust without such a live carrying threat at fly half? Freddie Steward is improving rapidly as an attacking link-man and decisive carrier, but is not necessarily a second playmaker in the George Furbank mould. Feyi-Waboso’s roaming, roving injections will also be much missed.

Still, though, opportunity knocks for both Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph. It is a year since Ojomoh won player of the match on his second cap against Argentina – having been clear work-ons, particularly in terms of the ground modern centres must now cover, Borthwick is keen to see him shine. “Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby. I think that’s undeniable. You can see what he can do with the ball in his hands,’ said Borthwick. ‘That’s one of the reasons why I’m looking forward to seeing him out there on Saturday.”

It is more than four years since Joseph, meanwhile, last pulled on an England shirt, and briefly, in Australia. He is rewarded for an outstanding start to the season with Gloucester, both at outside centre and on the wing “He starts on the wing but I’m encouraging him to get off his wing as much as he sees fit and is willing to do and able to do at the right opportunity. I see that he’s got an ability to go and find the ball and the big messaging is to back yourself.”

Japan are an evolving proposition with which to contend. Eddie Jones’s side are likely to bring a serious threat at the lineout, with Jack Cornelsen complementing the imposing lock duo of Harry Hockings and Warner Dearns as a third jumper, and jackalled more against Wales they have of late. Their 42 kicks per game are the most of any team in the Nations Championship, with good variety in that regard. England may nonetheless feel that they can enjoy a contestable kicking advantage, particularly against a Japanese back three that includes the diminutive but dangerous Kippei Ishida, and Riku Tokito, plucked from sevens to make his first professional 15-a-side appearance at Twickenham.

title: Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur set for $156,000 payday without playing a single match
article_text:
Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur narrowly missed out on qualification into the ATP Finals this year.

Both men have been a permanent fixture at the year-end tournament in recent years, with Fritz playing the event in three of the last four years.

De Minaur, meanwhile, has played the tournament in the last two years and even reached the semifinals of event in 2025, before losing to eventual winner Jannik Sinner.

Despite not qualifying, both de Minaur and Fritz are set to be alternates at the tournament and they will be paid handsomely for waiting in the wings.

The American and the Australian will need to help practice with the eight qualified players and be on hand if there is an injury or a withdrawal.

As a result of their alternate status, de Minaur and Fritz will be paid a very nice $156,000 and they might not have to play a single competitive match.

To put that fee into context, Fritz would only receive $128,016 if he won the Stockholm Open this week, so it’s a very important payday for both men.

Fritz has earned $3,700,373 in prize money across the year, but his ATP Finals alternate prize money will be his biggest payday outside of Grand Slams and Masters 1000s.

Likewise, De Minaur has claimed $4,166,407 in prize money this year, despite the fact he has performed poorly on the Grand Slam stage this term.

Fritz’s ATP Finals alternate place also makes his decision to play the Stockholm Open a whole lot more feasible, despite the fact it won’t help him qualify for the ATP Finals.

Many were bemused by Fritz’s decision to play the Stockholm Open, but he will need to stick around in Europe anyway to be an alternate at the ATP Finals, which takes place in Turin, Italy.

Not only will he gain an advantage on his ATP Finals rivals for the 2027 tournament, but he will remain sharp just in case he is called upon at the tournament.

Alternates have been needed sporadically throughout the years, with 15 players substituted in at the ATP Finals in the last 30 years.

David Nalbandian is arguably the most famous alternate in ATP Finals history, however, as he won the tournament while ranked world No 12 in the ATP Tour rankings.

He entered the tournament in 2005 as an alternate and defeated Roger Federer and Nikolay Davydenko in the knockout stages to lift the title.

title: Cricket titans get sponsorship boost
article_text:
Buoyed by having won 22 trophies and this year marking a 40th anniversary, South Africa’s unbeaten cricket champions Titans have every reason to celebrate.

Gaming company ZARbet, which has backed the club with a 12-month partnership, could renew the sponsorship after a year.

According to ZARbet CEO William Reyneke, the company’s partnership with the Titans formed “part of a broader approach and is not a once-off initiative”.

“Through ZARbet, we look for South African events and organisations that have genuine roots in their communities - where we can be actively involved, not simply placing our logo on a board,” said Reyneke.

“ZARbet is a local brand, built by South Africans for South Africans.

“And the Titans are as authentically South African.

“We share the Titans’ values of community, trust and transparency - as well as their ambition to succeed in the right way.

“This made the partnership a natural fit for us,” he added.

The ZARbet-Titans partnership enabled the club “to continue investing in its players, stadium and supporters”.

“For ZARbet, the partnership associates our brand with one of South Africa’s most successful cricket teams and gives us the opportunity to create memorable experiences for cricket fans,” said Reyneke.

He said all sponsorship contributions were allocated to a central funding pool, supporting shared services across the Titans organisation.

“This includes stadium management, amateur cricket through the Titans Cricket Union and the Sky Blues Trust, which supports women’s cricket and educational projects.

On ZARbet’s broader approach, Reyneke said: “Two recent examples demonstrate this approach. ZARbet is a sponsor of Lamb Champs, a competition that celebrates South Africa’s family farmers and the quality of locally produced lamb.

“The partnership appealed to us because it is proudly local, brings communities together and supports the people behind the product.

ZARbet was also one of the sponsors of Prime Fest, a festival centred around South African music and artists.

The common thread is simple: we back local. We will continue exploring opportunities in sport, entertainment and community events where there is a genuine alignment with our values and where our involvement can make a meaningful local difference. We will share further details as new partnerships are confirmed.”

Having bagged 22 trophies from March, the Titans has become the most successful team in South Africa, with big superstar players that have included batter Dewald Brevis, IPL big hitter Tabraiz Shamsi, Proteas spinner Keegan Petersen, test batter Dayyaan Galiem, Proteas all-rounder Eathan Bosch, fast bowler Leus du Plooy, left-hand batter Rivaldo Moonsamy and Sinethemba Qeshile.

Graham and Kinghorn return for Scotland as Leatherbarrow to debut vs Australia
article_text:
Scotland's record try scorer Darcy Graham returns to the Scotland side to face Australia at Murrayfield on Sunday as Gregor Townsend makes just two changes from the defeat to New Zealand.

Graham and his fellow British and Irish Lion Blair Kinghorn are both restored to the starting line-up, replacing Jamie Dobie and Kyle Rowe on the left wing and at fullback, respectively.

And there is a potential international debut for Ollie Leatherbarrow, with the former U20s cap named on the bench.

Dobie drops to the bench after an ineffective display against the All Blacks, while Rowe drops out of the matchday 23 altogether.

Elsewhere, Townsend has stuck with the same pack that started against New Zealand, meaning Rory Sutherland again gets the nod at loosehead prop, with Pierre Schoeman once more on the bench.

Gregor Brown, who was a fitness concern, has been passed fit to start, and Jack Dempsey gets another chance at number eight despite a quiet afternoon last weekend.
